{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "Conduct separate one-way ANOVAs for each continuous response variable (Time-to-Target, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, AD) with Stim Paradigm as the 5-level categorical factor",
    "For Success (binary: 0/1), use one-way ANOVA on the proportion or equivalently logistic regression framework; given the large sample (n=76655), ANOVA on the binary indicator is robust for detecting mean differences but logistic regression is preferred for proper variance structure",
    "Given severely unequal group sizes (Combined n=48846 vs Sham n=3505), use Welch's ANOVA or verify homogeneity of variance assumption; if violated, apply Welch correction or bootstrap methods",
    "Include Mouse as a blocking factor in a mixed-effects ANOVA or repeated-measures framework to account for 8 mice with unbalanced observations per mouse"
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "Following significant omnibus ANOVA results, conduct pairwise comparisons between all 10 pairs of stimulation paradigms",
    "Use Games-Howell post-hoc test for unequal variances and sample sizes, or Tukey HSD if variance homogeneity holds",
    "For Success (binary), use pairwise comparisons of proportions with appropriate standard error adjustments",
    "Focus comparisons on Sham vs active stimulation conditions and Combined vs unimodal conditions (ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only)"
  ],
  "multiple_comparison_strategy": "Benjamini-Hochberg FDR control for the 10 pairwise comparisons per response variable, with familywise error controlled across the 5 response variables using Bonferroni or Holm adjustment (total tests: 50 pairwise comparisons), or alternatively use hierarchical testing where omnibus ANOVA gates post-hoc tests",
  "predictive_model_recommendation": "Given that Stim Paradigm is categorical with 5 unordered levels, ordinary linear regression with dummy coding is appropriate for predicting continuous performance metrics from paradigm labels, but for predicting Stim Paradigm FROM the performance variables (the stated goal), this is a multiclass classification problem. Recommend: multinomial logistic regression with Stim Paradigm as response and the 5 performance variables as predictors, or alternatively random forest/multinomial naive Bayes for nonlinear relationships. The multinomial logistic regression is preferred for interpretability, with regularization (elastic net) given the large sample size and potential multicollinearity among predictors. Do not use ordinary linear regression to predict a categorical response.",
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Check homogeneity of variance with Levene's test; given unequal n (ratio >10:1), expect violation and plan Welch corrections",
    "Assess normality of residuals via Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk on subsamples; given n>75000, central limit theorem supports ANOVA robustness but extreme skew in Path Efficiency (max=29.8, mean=0.47) suggests log-transformation or robust methods",
    "Check for influential observations given extreme max values in Path Efficiency and Time-to-Target",
    "Verify independence assumption: likely violated due to repeated measures from 8 mice; use mixed-effects models with random intercept for Mouse",
    "For multinomial logistic regression: check IIA (independence of irrelevant alternatives) assumption and multicollinearity among predictors (VIF < 5)"
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham condition expected to show significantly lower Success (0.27 vs 0.67-0.78), higher Time-to-Target (4.68s vs 2.56-3.14s), lower Path Efficiency (0.31 vs 0.43-0.50), lower Average Speed (10.74 vs 11.97-12.83), and lower AD (0.24 vs 0.34-0.40) compared to all active stimulation paradigms",
    "Combined stimulation expected to outperform or match unimodal conditions, particularly showing highest Success (0.78) and lowest Time-to-Target (2.56s)",
    "Visual stimulation paradigms expected to differ: Bright Visual Only higher Success (0.78) than Dim Visual Only (0.67), with corresponding differences in Path Efficiency and AD",
    "ICMS Only and Dim Visual Only expected to show intermediate and similar performance profiles",
    "AD (angular dispersion) expected to be highest in Combined (0.40) and lowest in Sham (0.24), suggesting stimulation increases trajectory variability but improves performance"
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in group sizes (Combined 63.7% of data, Sham 4.6%) reduces power for Sham comparisons and may affect variance estimation",
    "No information on trial-level structure, temporal order, or learning effects across the 76,655 trials",
    "Missing data on trial duration, target distance, or other covariates that could explain Path Efficiency outliers (max=29.8)",
    "Binary Success variable analyzed alongside continuous metrics; different distributional assumptions required",
    "8 mice with unbalanced observations (SC21LM 10986 vs SC11LM 7233) may introduce subject-level confounds not fully addressable without mixed-effects modeling",
    "No replication information or cross-validation structure specified for predictive model evaluation"
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit a linear mixed-effects model for each continuous outcome with Stim Paradigm as fixed effect and Mouse as random intercept, followed by estimated marginal means and pairwise comparisons with Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom; simultaneously fit a multinomial logistic regression with elastic net regularization to predict Stim Paradigm from the 5 performance variables, using stratified 5-fold cross-validation to assess classification accuracy given class imbalance, and report confusion matrix with per-class precision/recall."
}
